mainText: Good morning. Here's the Tuesday, November 17 briefing. It's a cold, foggy start in Addieville, in the mid to upper 20s. By afternoon it turns sunny and mild, with a high near 59 degrees, a light south breeze, and no rain. Tonight is clear, with a low around 36. The warm-up continues, with a high near 63 on Wednesday, 67 on Thursday, and 69 on Friday. There's a 30 percent chance of rain late Saturday night. Local news: The county's recycling and trash plan meeting is tonight, from 6 to 7 P.M., at the courthouse in Nashville. It's the five-year plan update, and the public can attend. Sheriff's foreclosure auctions opened online yesterday for 115 West Elm Street in Okawville and 385 North Pine Street in Nashville. Around the region, two people were airlifted after a crash at Brubaker and Charleston roads northeast of Salem. Two more were hurt in Iuka when a car rolled over swerving to miss a deer, a good reminder with the rut and gun season here. Centralia has a boil order on the 1100 to 1200 blocks of North Lincoln Street, and about 1,200 people received free Thanksgiving dinners in Salem and Centralia. In St. Louis, aldermen voted 12 to 1 to put a measure on the April 2027 ballot that would let money from the 2017 sales tax help fund rapid bus service on the north-south corridor. The new westbound Chain of Rocks Bridge opening has slipped to next weekend. The state is also trying to get parts of the city's lawsuit over the state takeover of city police thrown out. The outcome of last week's county levy hearing still has not been posted. In local politics, the County Clerk is taking school board petitions through November 20, from 8 A.M. to 4 P.M., and on November 23 from 8 A.M. to 5 P.M. The Nashville Community High School District 99 board meets Wednesday at 6 P.M. in the Media Center, and will vote on approving its tax levy and on a change to the science-lab renovation. Nashville Community Consolidated School District 49 holds its hearing on raising administrative costs on Tuesday, November 24, at 8 P.M.

National and world news. The Commerce Department now requires licenses for overseas data centers that serve Chinese companies, closing a loophole that let them rent advanced A.I. chips remotely. Exports of those chips to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, Indonesia, and Brazil also need licenses now. An update on last week's F.A.A. ground stop: more than 12,000 flights were canceled over the weekend. Transportation Secretary Duffy blamed a contractor's wiring upgrade and asked Congress for another 50 billion dollars for air traffic control. Democrats point out that most of the 12 and a half billion dollars already approved has not been spent. In the Middle East, Yemen's government pulled troops back to defend Aden as the Houthis advance, and the U.S. sent a third aircraft carrier to the region. President Trump heads to Asia for Thursday's meeting with Xi and Putin. In Illinois, police arrested a suspect in the Peoria ethanol-plant bomb case. The veto session opened, with a Bears stadium bill and who pays for data centers' power-grid costs on the agenda. The state faces a projected 2.3 billion dollar budget gap next year.

In sports, the Blues, now 9-9-2, host the Ducks tonight at 7 P.M. on ESPN Plus, after Saturday's 4-1 loss to Florida. The Broncos, at 7-2, are back from the bye and preparing for the Raiders on Sunday. Brandon Jones and Hufanga are listed out, while Waddle and Moss are questionable. Okawville boys basketball has its Blue and White scrimmage November 22, and opens November 25 at Gibault. For Illinois hunting, deer archery pauses after Thursday, November 19. The firearm season runs November 20 to 22, and archery reopens November 23.

In gaming, Rockstar pushed a second pre-launch patch for G.T.A. 6, about 600 megabytes on PlayStation 5 and 1.6 gigabytes on Xbox, ahead of Thursday's launch. In Modern Warfare 4, Monday's update cut the Drill Charge's long-range damage by 75 percent, and the Natural Concealment camo event runs through November 23. On the markets, Monday was a rough day. The Dow fell 1.41 percent to 51,608. The S and P 500 fell 1.92 percent to 7,417. The Nasdaq fell 2.49 percent to 24,510. Chip stocks led the drop on the new export rule, worries about Nvidia's leadership, and caution ahead of the Anthropic I.P.O. Nvidia closed at 156 dollars and 14 cents, down 4.1 percent. It reports after the close today, its first report without Huang. Analysts expect about 109 billion dollars in revenue, and options are pricing in a move of roughly 7 to 8 percent either way. Intel fell 7 percent to 55.47. Oracle fell 5 percent to 119.09. Caterpillar fell about 5 percent, to around 570. J.P. Morgan closed at 338.21, Casey's around 706, and Caly around 16.96. Exxon fell 2.1 percent to 166.98, and Chevron fell 1.3 percent to 217.14, as oil slid to about 86 dollars. Worth watching: Anthropic prices its I.P.O. Wednesday at an expected 70 to 78 dollars a share, under the ticker A.N.T., and starts trading Thursday. A.M.D. fell 5.6 percent to about 504, and tonight's Nvidia numbers could set its direction too. Retail sales data also comes out today. This is not financial advice.

titleText: Verse and word of the day
mainText: The verse of the day is Ecclesiastes chapter 4, verses 9 and 10. Two are better than one, because they have a good reward for their toil. For if they fall, one will lift up his fellow. Whether it's your coworkers today or the people you spend the evening with, be the one who lifts someone up. The word of the day is sanguine. It means staying optimistic, especially when things look tough, like on a red day on Wall Street.
